findings.title: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities duplicates useCanSilence logic and may fetch folder twice
findings.body: The new `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` hook (lines 287-337) reads `useCanSilenceInFolder(rule?.folderUid)` while the legacy `useCanSilence(rule)` (line 560) also reads `useFolder(folderUID)` internally. This means `useFolder` is fetched both directly here and via `useCanSilenceInFolder` -> `useFolderPermissions` -> `useFolder`. For every Grafana rule in the list view this triggers two redundant RTKQ/cache lookups for the folder per row. With ~80 rules on the list page this roughly doubles the folder lookups the page used to make.

findings.title: useRulerRuleAbility still called from list view with rule=undefined
findings.body: `RuleActionsButtons.V2` is now invoked with only `promRule` from the Grafana list view (see `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`, line ~47, where it is rendered with `<RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ...>` and no `rule` prop). However the component unconditionally invokes `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` on line 53. With `rule === undefined` the hook falls into `useAllRulerRuleAbities -> useIsRuleEditable`, which still performs ruler availability/work per rule row even though the goal of the PR is to remove ruler from the list view. The list-view call sites should pass a sentinel (e.g. `skipToken`) or branch the call so ruler abilities are not evaluated for Grafana list items.

findings.title: Both ruler and prom ability hooks always execute
findings.body: `AlertRuleMenu` always invokes both `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...)` (line 57) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(... ? promRule : skipToken, ...)` (line 73), even though in the new list view `rulerRule` is undefined. `useRulerRuleAbilities` -> `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` -> `useIsRuleEditable` still performs per-group ruler availability/RBAC checks for every rule rendered by the list. For 80 rules that is 80 ruler-availability lookups, defeating the PR's stated goal of removing ruler from the list view. The component should branch on the available data source (or accept a `skipToken` for the ruler side) when invoked from the list view.

findings.title: Stale comment about ruler preload after removing the dispatch
findings.body: The block in `useGrafanaGroupsGenerator` (around line 82-95) previously also dispatched a `getGrafanaRulerGroup` prefetch; this PR removed that dispatch but left the comment `// This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded`. The comment now references behavior that no longer exists (no ruler preload) and should be updated or removed.

findings.title: isProvisionedPromRule returns false for non-Grafana prom rules via incorrect truthy coercion
skipToken symbol conflicts with other skip-token conventions in this codebase
findings.body: A new top-level `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token')` is declared in this file (line 380). RTK Query already exports a `skipToken` symbol and the codebase imports it elsewhere via `@reduxjs/toolkit`. Defining a second, unrelated `skipToken` in this module is a recipe for shadowing/import-collision bugs: any code that does `import { skipToken } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query'` near this module, or relies on the RTKQ skip semantics, will get a different value. The component-level usages here happen to compare by identity against the local symbol, but future refactors (or merging imports) will be confusing. Prefer reusing the existing RTK Query `skipToken`.

findings.title: useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable loses memoization when rule is undefined
findings.body: `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns the early-return object `{ isEditable: false, isRemovable: false, loading: false }` directly when `!rule || !folderUID`. Returning a fresh object on every render breaks referential equality for `loading`/`isEditable`/`isRemovable` that the parent memo `useMemo(() => ..., [..., isEditable, isRemovable, ...])` watches. Every parent render will rebuild the abilities map. Wrap the empty case in a `useMemo(() => ({...}), [])` (or hoist a module constant) so the deps array can short-circuit.

findings.title: Redundant type narrowing for promAlertingRule
findings.body: Inside the alerting-rule branch, `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` has just been checked true, but the code then re-checks `rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` to construct `promAlertingRule`. This second check is redundant (and silently nulls out valid Grafana alerting rules if their `type` field were ever different). It also means `promAlertingRule` may be `undefined` even though we are in the alerting branch, leading to a `state` of `undefined` being passed into `AlertRuleListItem`. Either drop the redundant check or rely on it exclusively.

findings.title: mimirDataSource declared but unused after parameter change
findings.body: `const { dataSource: mimirDs } = mimirDataSource();` is added at the top of the test file (line 37) and passed into `getCloudRule({ name: 'Cloud' }, { rulesSource: mimirDs })`. The tests do not exercise any cloud-specific behavior beyond checking that Edit/Delete buttons are absent, which is the same expected behavior regardless of datasource. The added dependency is dead - the mock provider for `mimirDs` is set up but never asserted against, so the test does not regress-protect anything that the previous signature didn't already cover.

findings.title: Test destructures rulerRule but never asserts the new prom-rule abilities path
findings.body: In the `creating/deleting states` describe block, the test creates `creatingRule` and `deletingRule` by destructuring `{ promRule, ...creatingRule }` and `{ rulerRule, ...deletingRule }`. After this PR, the list-view rendering path no longer reads `rulerRule` for abilities, but the tests override the abilities via `useRulerRuleAbilities` (line 172) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (line 175) in such a way that everything is `[true, true]`. The 'Creating'/'Deleting' rendering path that used `RuleOperationListItem` has been removed entirely from `GrafanaGroupLoader` (it no longer fetches the ruler group), so the `deletingRule` case (where no `promRule` exists) cannot actually render through the new code path. The test now passes only because everything is mocked to `[true, true]`; it does not catch the real regression that 'pending deletion' (prom-only) UI is gone. This is a meaningful test gap introduced by the PR.

findings.title: Delete menu item guarded only by canDelete && rulerRule
findings.body: The Delete entry is conditioned on `canDelete && rulerRule` (line 165). With this PR, on the Grafana list view `rulerRule` is `undefined` and `canDelete` is allowed via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (the Grafana branch returns `true`), so Delete will not render for Grafana rules in the list view. The component should accept a Deletable identifier (the same way `RuleActionsButtons.V2.getEditableIdentifier` does) and gate Delete on having a deletable identifier (or on `canDelete` alone) - otherwise deleting a Grafana rule from the list view becomes impossible without going through a different code path.

findings.title: Loses 'Deleting' UI for in-flight prom-only deletions
findings.body: The previous implementation rendered `<RuleOperationListItem operation={RuleOperation.Deleting}>` for `promOnlyRules` - rules that existed in Prometheus but not in Ruler. The new implementation iterates only over `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` and no longer considers Ruler, so rules currently being deleted (still in Prom, gone from Ruler) will simply disappear from the list view without any 'Deleting' indicator. The PR removes functionality that was documented as needed for eventual consistency between Ruler and Prometheus (see comment in `prometheusGroupsGenerator.ts`). The PR claim that 'Grafana Prometheus rules should be strongly consistent now' (former matchRules comment) is asserted in code, but the UI safety net for inconsistency is gone.

findings.title: Declare Incident menu passes empty URL
findings.body: `{shouldShowDeclareIncidentButton && <DeclareIncidentMenuItem title={promRule.name} url={''} />}` passes `url=''` to the menu item. With the ruler data (and presumably any annotation/labels-derived URL) no longer passed through here, the Declare Incident flow now navigates to the empty URL. This may or may not be a regression, but the URL is not the rule's view URL as one might expect; either the rule's `view` URL should be passed or this should be flagged as incomplete behavior.
